oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: elevated 5xxs from serving-runtime (eu-west-1, gpu-pool-3). Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOMs during streaming/decode. Affected model variants: rw-7b-chat / rw-7b-qa. Paging @eng-oncall and @raj (eng-runtime).

raj (eng-runtime): taking this. I see ~30% increase in dropped streams in last 8m.

maria (eng-sre): observed node flaps too? metrics show nodes 11-14 cycling containers. attaching quick tail from decode logs.

sre-ivy: paste logs:```
[2026-03-15T02:13:42Z] decode_step: CUDA out of memory when allocating 1.2GB for attention_kv
[2026-03-15T02:13:42Z] pid=4321 node=gpu-pool-3-node-12 model=rw-7b-chat request_id=abc123 stream=true
[2026-03-15T02:13:42Z] container crashed: OOM; restarting container
```

raj (eng-runtime): thanks. early hypothesis: runaway generation due to malformed client max_tokens or missing per-client cap causing unbounded streaming, KV cache blowup. Also see repeated requests with max_tokens=100000 in logs.

josh (eng-ml): that matches a regressed client-side SDK I saw yesterday in a Canary — missing guard when user sends {"max_tokens":null} and our handler falls back to server-default of 1e6 in some code paths. I'll paste the offending snippet.

josh (eng-ml): ```python
# problematic fallback in request handler
def normalize_request(req):
    mt = req.get("max_tokens")
    if mt is None:
        mt = CONFIG.get("default_max_tokens")  # used to be 512, accidentally set to 1000000 in last deploy
    return mt
```

maria (eng-sre): ok that's a big signal. Immediate mitigation options: 1) patch and rollback the handler config (quick) 2) enforce per-request token hard-cap at routing layer (hotfix) 3) temporarily cordon gpu-pool-3 nodes and shift traffic to gpu-pool-1 (capacity available) 4) enable fallback to quantized model variant (lower VRAM).

eng-oncall: taking traffic control. I'll set routing policy to hard-cap tokens at 2048 for all streaming requests from the edge for now. executing:```bash
rb-route update --region eu-west-1 --token-hard-cap 2048 --match streaming=true
```

ops-bot: command accepted. Changes applied in 18s. Active routes updated.

lucas (prodops): also throttling new sessions to gpu-pool-3 by 60% to reduce churn. If this holds we'll avoid more OOMs while we fix handler.

raj (eng-runtime): starting temp remediation: kill/recycle containers on nodes 11-14, flush KV caches for model rw-7b-chat. Commands:```bash
rbctl drain node gpu-pool-3-node-12 --grace 15s
rbctl restart container 4321 --force
rbctl kvcache purge --model rw-7b-chat --nodes gpu-pool-3
```

maria (eng-sre): observed reduce in OOMs after route hard-cap + kv purge. error rate down from 18% 5xx -> 2.5% over 6m. Some customers still seeing dropped streams if they had in-flight runaway sessions.

tina (customer-success): which customers hit? need list for outreach. saw CS ticket from "acme-payments" reporting truncated responses and dropped streams.

raj (eng-runtime): acme-payments had 4 requests with max_tokens=999999 in the logs. contacting them and suspending the long-running sessions server-side.

raj (eng-runtime): quick patch ready to push: revert default_max_tokens to 512 and add server-side clamp to 8192. Will submit PR and request emergency deploy.

sre-ivy: please coordinate canary to gpu-pool-1 first, then bounce the handler service.

josh (eng-ml): note: we should also add a safety limiter in the decode loop to abort when KV cache > 12GB for a session. I'll open a follow-up PR after hotfix.

eng-oncall: rolling hotfix now (canary -> 5% traffic gpu-pool-1). watch for regressions.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff scheduled to night shift @eng-oncall in 45m. PagerDuty alert will remain until incident is resolved.

maria (eng-sre): post-fix metrics: 5xx -> 0.8%, OOM events per node -> 0. Traffic back to normal levels. We still have ~12 in-flight sessions that ended prematurely; we're compensating with retries.

tina (customer-success): flagging acme-payments for priority outreach. I'll send a templated apology + explanation and offer replay for affected requests.

lucas (prodops): we should consider automated rollback of config that sets default_max_tokens > 8192. I'll file infra ticket.

raj (eng-runtime): creating incident ticket: INC-2026-0457. Summary: runaway streaming due to handler default_max_tokens misconfig -> GPU OOMs -> container crashes and request drops. Root cause: bad default changed in last deploy. Mitigation: route hard-cap, kv purge, container restart, hotfix to revert default and add clamp.

maria (eng-sre): handoff notes for night shift: monitor gpu-pool-3 for recurring OOMs, watch decode OOM metric and node restarts, ensure token-hard-cap remains active. If OOMs reappear escalate to oncall-senior.

eng-oncall: acknowledged. Handoff complete. leaving detailed runbook steps in INC-2026-0457.

raj (eng-runtime): followups: add unit test for normalize_request behavior, add integration test for streaming token clamp, bake safety limiter in decode.

maria (eng-sre): postmortem owner: raj + maria. target writeup by 48h.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Will auto-close when stable for 24h.
